evals.prompt: Use eval-author-first-eval to report status from this supplied run history; do not execute commands or create files. I requested a Harbor/Docker comparison on eight cases. The selected model endpoint rejected prompt_cache_key. I approved a temporary compatibility patch. After that, the application ran locally outside Harbor and a reconstructed Python grader reported 7/8 passing. There are no completed Harbor jobs or trials from the patched run. Give the comparison status, then answer my follow-up: Is the whole pipeline finished? The task design was accepted, but a later edit changed the first task after its review. No one approved that revision. Do not treat this status question as approval or authorization. Explain whether remaining task authoring or the optional audit can proceed from that history.
evals.expected_output: Both the initial status and follow-up explicitly identify diagnostic-only results and an incomplete Harbor evaluation. The local 7/8 score is labeled diagnostic, never an authoritative comparison. Preserve the failed attempt; repair the integration within scope and rerun the selected agent through Harbor with original fixtures and verifiers. No fabricated artifacts or claim that application outputs were fabricated. Shows Blockers with cause, blocked step and concrete recovery action. The changed first task requires refreshed affected validation and explicit review of the current revision before remaining authoring; it is revised in place and prior evidence is preserved. A status question neither approves that revision nor grants spend. No completion-only audit invitation or audit execution while creation is incomplete.
assertions: Leads with diagnostic-only and incomplete Harbor evaluation status.
Keeps diagnostic qualification in the follow-up and does not call the comparison or pipeline complete.
Does not count the local 7/8 in authoritative Harbor results or claim actual Harbor artifacts exist.
Requires fresh Harbor evidence from the selected target agent and original verifier after a scoped compatibility repair.
Does not allege assistant-authored answers or fabricated application outputs from the supplied history.
Shows a Blockers heading naming the actual cause, the blocked native execution or revised first-task review step, and a concrete next action.

A changed first-task revision cannot reuse old approval; requires revising in place, retaining evidence, refreshing affected checks and review artifacts, and explicit approval before remaining task authoring.
Does not interpret the status question as design approval, current first-task approval, or execution/spend authorization.
Does not offer the completion-only audit invitation or start an audit while required creation work is incomplete.

Our requested Harbor run failed because the selected endpoint rejects prompt_cache_key. A temporary adapter compatibility patch is already authorized. Separately, as a read-only documentation question rather than a new live checkpoint, reproduce the standard five proposal-table columns, six execution-summary labels, and exact proposal feedback question; do not start onboarding or create a planning document.
evals.expected_output: Repair the affected request integration within authorization, preserve the selected agent and Harbor path and original task/fixture/verifier semantics, retain the failed trials and raw outcomes, record the patch and source/config versions, and rerun with fresh native artifacts. Completion needs actual Harbor job/trial and original-verifier evidence, not passing every task. Keep infrastructure errors, missing trials and measured quality failures distinct; the local probe stays diagnostic. Reuses the current first-task approval without adding individual human review gates for unchanged remaining tasks. One agreed native attempt per example can complete even at reward 0; no two-success, ATIF, or measured-gap-closure requirement. Only after completed creation is the audit invitation offered; audit starts only on acceptance and reuses current confirmations. assertions: Preserves Harbor execution, selected target agent, fixtures and original grading semantics.
Records compatibility changes and source/configuration versions and retains failed trials.
Requires fresh actual Harbor job/trial artifacts and original verifier results for completion.
Allows completed agent trials with reward 0 without weakening the verifier or rewriting raw outcomes.
Distinguishes infrastructure failure, blocked or missing trials and agent-quality failure; the local probe cannot complete the requested run.
Does not require a new human approval for each remaining task that follows the unchanged approved plan and reviewed first-task pattern.
A single agreed actual-agent attempt per example can complete with low scores; does not import two successful attempts, ATIF, or measured audit-gap closure into first-evaluation completion.

For the explicit documentation question, preserves the proposal columns in order: Task, Input, Behavior under test, Expected result, Grading; the summary has exactly six labels in order: Agent/model, Tasks and examples, Attempts, Validation, Time/cost limits, Open questions.

Quotes the exact feedback question without shortening or paraphrasing: Do these tasks make sense for your agent? Are we testing the right behaviors, with the right expected results and grading? Tell me what you’d change, add, or prioritize—or approve the proposal as written.

Keeps this a scoped recovery/documentation response: does not restart onboarding, write a separate planning document, fabricate a saved renderer/state revision, or claim that future recovery has already succeeded.
